grammar.title: Reflexive Verbs and Daily Meal Expressions
grammar.explanation: Italian uses specific expressions for meals: 'fare colazione' (to have breakfast), 'pranzare' (to have lunch), 'cenare' (to have dinner). Cooking verbs follow regular conjugation patterns: cucinare (-are), bollire (-ire), friggere (-ere). Note that 'friggere' is irregular in the past participle: 'fritto'. The expression 'mi piace + infinitive' means 'I like to...' and is commonly used with cooking verbs.
